lines.text: Why you couldn't survive being an emperor penguin dad.
First, you walk up to seventy miles across the ice just to reach the colony.
Your partner lays one egg, hands it to you, and leaves for two months.
You balance it on your feet. If it touches the ice for a few minutes, it freezes.
It's minus forty out here, with winds up to a hundred miles an hour.
So you huddle with thousands of other dads, taking turns on the freezing edge.
And you don't eat. For four months. You lose almost half your body weight.
When the chick hatches, you feed it milk from your own throat.
But that's not even the worst part.
Giant petrels circle the colony, waiting for the weak ones.
And when you finally reach the water to eat, a leopard seal is waiting.
But this is your absolute worst nightmare.
If the sea ice breaks up too early, your chick falls into the ocean before its waterproof feathers grow in.
In 2022, that happened at four colonies. Almost every chick was lost.
